title: Smoked Baked Beans for the Crew
displayTitle: Smoked Baked Beans for the Crew
seoTitle: Smoked Baked Beans for the Crew | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: The pot that makes every BBQ plate feel complete
subtitle: Molasses-brown sugar beans with burnt-end depth for ten
description: Adapted from classic pit-style baked beans tradition (BBQ Pit Boys, Amazing Ribs): canned beans simmer with molasses, brown sugar, and bacon, then smoke at 275°F for 2 hours until thick and smoky.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Baked Beans for the Crew in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch vegetarian. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Render bacon
steps.instruction: Cook diced bacon in a pot until crisp. Remove half for topping; leave rest with fat. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sweat onion
steps.instruction: Cook diced onion in bacon fat until soft, about 6 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build bean base
steps.instruction: Add beans, ketchup, molasses, brown sugar, mustard, vinegar, Worcestershire, and BBQ sauce. Simmer 20 minutes until starting to thicken. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smoke at 275°F
steps.instruction: Transfer to foil pans. Smoke uncovered at 275°F 2 hours, stirring once, until thick and smoky. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Cover with foil and hold at 170°F until service. Top with reserved crisp bacon before serving. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Beans in a pot with ladle alongside any smoked meat. Call it the hall pot—everyone gets a scoop. Target 165°F for any egg-based components at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F for any egg-based components. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered at 325°F until 165°F. Fold into burritos with pulled pork. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Uncovered smoke thickens the pot—stir the edges so they don't crust.
Mix bean varieties for texture; all pintos turn mushy.
Reserved crisp bacon goes on at service or it softens.
tonightSpread: Smoked beans in a Dutch oven with ladle.
Crisp bacon bits in a side bowl for topping.
leftovers: Top loaded nachos with beans and cheese.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Beans hold forever at 170°F, stretch any meat plate, and taste better the longer they sit on the smoker.
mealPrepNotes: Simmer base on the stove, then transfer to foil pans on the smoker. Hold covered at 170°F up to 3 hours. Stir before service.
